messages:
owen: Hey @people-ops — quick one. I relocated from Ireland to the US on 2026-02-10 and updated my address in the portal, but my 03/15 paycheck shows Irish PAYE withheld *and* US federal withholding. PTO payout (PR-2026-04321) also got taxed at Irish rate. Can someone check if my country code was flipped mid-payrun?

maria-hr: @owen thanks for flagging. Sorry about the hassle. Can you paste the payroll ID and the pay date? I'll ping payroll right away. :eyes:

owen: Payroll ID: PR-2026-04321, pay date 2026-03-15. Also my relocation form was approved 2026-02-09 (manager+people-ops).

jamie-payroll: taking a look. First guess is the employee record change came through after the payroll cut-off for March, so the run taxed as IE. If you moved before cut-off we can reverse and reprocess. Need last 4 of SSN and confirmation of US tax residency start date to request tax reclaim.

owen: SSN last4 4821. US tax residency start date 2026-02-10.

lee-finance: Adding context — for cross-border midyear moves we usually: 1) reverse the affected payrun, 2) re-run as US-taxable, 3) file for refund with Irish revenue if PAYE was paid, and 4) issue corrected US docs (W-2/W-2c) if needed. Will coordinate with Jamie.

jamie-payroll: Created ticket and kicked off payrun reversal. Ticket #PAY-9876. PayrollBot should post the link.

PayrollBot: Created ticket PAY-9876 and internal payrun job. Link: https://tickets.redwood/payroll/PAY-9876 :white_check_mark:

jamie-payroll: Next steps for @owen:
```
- We'll reverse PR-2026-04321 (expected reversal posted in 1-2 business days)
- Re-run the March pay as US-taxable (same net hours)
- Submit refund claim to Irish revenue for the PAYE withheld (timeline varies)
- If US withholding ends up different, we'll issue a W-2c at year-end or sooner if necessary
```

maria-hr: @owen I also verified the relocation approval date. Your benefits change effective 2026-02-10, so payroll change should have been effective for March but it looks like it missed the cutoff. Sorry — we'll fast-track.

owen: Appreciate it. Rough ETA on when the corrected net will land in my account? Need to plan rent.

lee-finance: If reversal + re-run go smoothly we aim for the corrected payment in the next payroll cycle (04/01). If refund from Irish revenue is required for PAYE, that's a separate reclaim (may take weeks). We'll offset any shortfall in next paycheck if there is a timing gap.

jamie-payroll: Confirmed: reversal queued — if no blockers expect re-run by 03/31. I'll DM you once reversal posts and again when re-run is complete.

owen: Thanks all. One more Q — will this trigger a separate tax form for Ireland? I just want to keep records clean.

maria-hr: Good question. For payroll-side, you might get a payslip amendment for March showing reversal and corrected run. If Irish PAYE refund is issued, that will be separate correspondence. We'll include notes in your employee file.

lee-finance: We'll also flag for year-end reporting team — if anything requires a P45/P60 style document for Ireland we will surface it, but primary deliverable for US reporting will be the W-2 (or W-2c if we amend).

jamie-payroll: Action items: jamie -> process reversal; lee -> prepare short-term offset plan if reclaim delays; maria -> update HR record with notes and confirm with @owen when re-run completes.

owen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
